question: Does genome-derived per-strain mu_max (gRodon) improve on the tuned uniform mu_max=0.6 cap? -- the validation-on-Clark of genome priors.
verdict: NEGATIVE: per-strain gRodon mu_max is WORSE than a uniform cap on both metrics, even rescaled to the same median -- the per-strain PATTERN hurts (interaction corr goes slightly negative).
mechanism: gRodon predicts the Bacteroidetes as the SLOWEST growers (BT 0.086, BY 0.099, BC 0.107 -- weak codon bias), but they are exactly the DM38 DOMINATORS (highest OD/yield). A per-strain cap throttles the real dominators hardest, inverting the competitive structure. Clark composition is YIELD-driven, not growth-RATE-driven; gRodon predicts optimal-condition growth RATE, which here ANTI-correlates with competitive success -- so it is the wrong prior for this regime. The uniform cap wins because it moderates the winner-take-all INSTABILITY without imposing a wrong per-strain rate ranking.
implication: For data-free generalization, the transferable knob is a UNIFORM physiological mu_max (~0.5-0.6/h, a defensible gut-anaerobe default), NOT per-strain genome growth-rate predictions. gRodon does not help in a yield-driven community. (gRodon may still matter in rate-limited/ chemostat regimes -- untested here.)
